rationale: The child question's source revision named one unmeasured exception: a cluster whose nodes do not share timer settings, because ValidateConfig enforces the lease/ heartbeat/ election relation per node rather than across the cluster, so a follower may be configured to campaign sooner than the leader's lease expires. That exception is now testable with a hand-built cluster that gives each node its own configuration, and the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence, produced the overlap the exception predicts: with the leader on a 50ms lease and the other voters on a 20ms election timeout, a competing leader appeared 29ms after the partition and the cut-off leader still obtained eight confirmations afterwards, while the uniform control produced no competing leader during the window and no confirmation after one. This submission reopens the child question for that revision and submits the probe so the overlap rests on a retained receipt rather than on a dry run.

resume_conditions: Retained execution of the mixed-timer probe decides whether the confirmation window really overlaps a competing leader when per-node timers differ.

scope.description: Two trials on hand-built four-node clusters in one process, because the cluster helper cannot give nodes different settings. In the mixed trial the leader-to-be carries the slow settings (50ms heartbeat, election and lease) while the other three nodes carry fast ones (10ms heartbeat, 20ms election, 5ms lease); in the control every node carries the slow settings. In both trials the slow node is made leader through a normal leadership transfer, one node is demoted to nonvoter with DemoteVoter so the cut-off leader has a peer whose acknowledgement can be counted, the leader and the nonvoter are then isolated from the two remaining voters in both directions, and the leader is verified repeatedly while the harness watches for a competing leader among those voters.
assumptions: Per-node configurations are legal: ValidateConfig is applied per node, and nothing in the captured snapshot requires the cluster to share timer values. The mixed trial therefore represents a cluster whose nodes drifted apart or were rolled out with different settings, not a configuration the library rejects.
Each node is bootstrapped with the same configuration, which is how the target's own multi-node tests create clusters.
The leader is forced onto the slow node by a normal LeadershipTransferToServer so that the lease under test belongs to the leader rather than to a node that happened to win the first election.
Verification is driven through the same channel the exported API uses, and a competing leader is detected by reading the two isolated nodes' states.
The dry run is native feedback only; the retained execution is what will be interpreted.
excluded: No application read is served, so the overlap is a fact about the confirmation and a competing leader's existence, not about a value returned to a client.
No on-disk store, no network transport and no multi-process execution.
The probe does not search over timer combinations; it contrasts the two configurations named above.

parameters.trials: trial 0 mixed timers (leader 50ms lease, voters 20ms election), trial 1 uniform timers (all nodes 50ms)
parameters.recorded_operands: leader_lease_ms, voter_election_ms, voter_election_shorter_than_lease, polls, confirmations, last_confirmation_ms, first_peer_leader_ms, confirmations_after_peer_leader, confirmation_after_peer_leader, leader_stepped_down, leader_term, peer_term, leader_applied_index

experiment.prefix: Each trial builds four nodes by hand: an in-memory transport per node, all pairs connected, one in-memory store serving as both log and stable store per node, an in-memory snapshot store and a MockFSM, each node bootstrapped with the same configuration and then started with its own Config. The harness waits for any leader, transfers leadership to the slow node through the exported API and waits until that node reports Leader, demotes the fourth node to nonvoter with DemoteVoter and waits for the change to settle, records a healthy baseline verification, applies one command, and then disconnects the leader and the nonvoter from the two remaining voters in both directions using the transports' Disconnect. From that moment it polls the verification path every 2ms while the leader still reports Leader, recording each outcome, while separately reading whether either isolated node reports Leader; it stops when the leader is no longer Leader and emits one summary event carrying the counts, the last confirmation's elapsed time, the first competing leader's elapsed time, how many confirmations followed a competing leader, the terms of the leader and of an isolated node, and the configured lease and election values that classify the trial. Only the TestAssurance-prefixed test in this harness is selected and no production file is modified.

comparisons.description: When a voter can campaign before the leader's lease expires, the cut-off leader still obtains confirmations after a competing leader exists.
Control: with every node on the same settings no competing leader exists while the cut-off leader still confirms.
